drivingQuestion: From which verses is it derived that God influences human conduct, that Moses spoke impertinently, and that abundance of good caused Israel's sin?
outcomeNote: aggadic chain: alternative prooftexts sit side by side without adjudication

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אִלְמָלֵא שָׁלֹשׁ מִקְרָאוֹת הַלָּלוּ נִתְמוֹטְטוּ רַגְלֵיהֶם שֶׁל שׂוֹנְאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
segments.en: Similarly, «Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: Had it not been for these three verses, the legs of the enemies of Israel,» a euphemism for Israel itself, «would have collapsed, as» Israel would have been unable to withstand God’s judgment.

segments.he: חַד דִּכְתִיב: ״וַאֲשֶׁר הֲרֵעֹתִי״, וְחַד דִּכְתִיב: ״הִנֵּה כַחֹמֶר בְּיַד הַיּוֹצֵר כֵּן אַתֶּם בְּיָדִי בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל״, וְחַד דִּכְתִיב: ״וַהֲסִרֹתִי אֶת לֵב הָאֶבֶן מִבְּשַׂרְכֶם וְנָתַתִּי לָכֶם לֵב בָּשָׂר״.
segments.en: «One» is the verse just mentioned in which «it is written: “Those whom I have dealt in wickedness.” And one» is the verse in which «it is written: “Behold, like clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in My hand, house of Israel”» (Jeremiah 18:6). «And one» is the verse in which «it is written:» “And I will give you a new heart and a new spirit I will place within you, «and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and I will give you a heart of flesh”» (Ezekiel 36:26). These three verses indicate that God influences a person’s decisions, and therefore one does not have sole responsibility for his actions.

segments.he: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״וְאֶת רוּחִי אֶתֵּן בְּקִרְבְּכֶם וְעָשִׂיתִי אֵת אֲשֶׁר בְּחֻקַּי תֵּלֵכוּ״.
segments.en: «Rav Pappa said» there is a clearer proof «from here: “And I will place My spirit within you and I will cause you to walk in My statutes,» and you will observe My decrees and do them” (Ezekiel 36:27).

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מֹשֶׁה הֵטִיחַ דְּבָרִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל מֹשֶׁה אֶל ה׳״ אַל תִּקְרֵי ״אֶל ה׳״, אֶלָּא ״עַל ה׳״.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Elazar said: Moses» also «spoke impertinently toward» God «on High, as it is stated» in the verse following the sin of those who murmured against God in the desert: «“And Moses prayed to the Lord» and the fire subsided” (Numbers 11:2), and this verse is interpreted homiletically: «Do not read to [el] the Lord,» but rather «onto [al] the Lord,» which indicates that he spoke impertinently.

segments.he: שֶׁכֵּן דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב קוֹרִין לָאַלְפִין עַיְינִין, וְלָעַיְינִין אַלְפִין.
segments.en: The Gemara explains the basis for this interpretation: «As» the Sages «of the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov would» indiscriminately «read alef as ayin and ayin as alef» and in this case transforming el into al.

segments.he: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמְרִי, מֵהָכָא: ״וְדִי זָהָב״.
segments.en: The Sages of «the school of Rabbi Yannai,» however, «say» proof that Moses spoke impertinently toward God on High is derived «from here,» Moses’ rebuke at the beginning of Deuteronomy: «“And Di Zahav”» (Deuteronomy 1:1). This is an entry in a list of places where Moses had spoken to Israel. As there was no place encountered by that name, it is interpreted as an allusion to another matter.

segments.he: מַאי ״וְדִי זָהָב״? אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: כָּךְ אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, בִּשְׁבִיל כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב שֶׁהִשְׁפַּעְתָּ לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ ״דַּי״ — הוּא גָּרַם שֶׁעָשׂוּ אֶת הָעֵגֶל.
segments.en: We must clarify: «What is» the meaning of «and Di Zahav?» The Sages of «the school of Rabbi Yannai said that Moses said the following before the Holy One, Blessed be He,» to atone for Israel after the sin of the Golden Calf: «Master of the Universe, because of the gold and silver that you lavished upon Israel» during the exodus from Egypt «until they said enough [dai];» it was this wealth «that caused» Israel «to make the» Golden «Calf.»

segments.he: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: אֵין אֲרִי נוֹהֵם מִתּוֹךְ קוּפָּה שֶׁל תֶּבֶן אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ קוּפָּה שֶׁל בָּשָׂר.
segments.en: Establishing a general moral principle, the Sages «the school of Rabbi Yannai said: A lion does not roar» standing «over a basket of straw» from which he derives no pleasure, «but» he roars standing «over a basket of meat,» as he only roars when satiated.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: מָשָׁל לְאָדָם שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ פָּרָה כְּחוּשָׁה וּבַעֲלַת אֵבָרִים, הֶאֱכִילָהּ כַּרְשִׁינִין וְהָיְתָה מְבַעֶטֶת בּוֹ. אָמַר לָהּ: מִי גָּרַם לִיךְ שֶׁתְּהֵא מְבַעֶטֶת בִּי — אֶלָּא כַּרְשִׁינִין שֶׁהֶאֱכַלְתִּיךְ.
segments.en: Similarly, «Rabbi Oshaya said:» This is «comparable to a person who had a lean, but large-limbed cow.» At one point, «he fed it lupines,» a choice food, «and» soon thereafter the cow «was kicking him. He said to» the cow: «Who caused you» to begin «kicking me if not the lupines I fed you?» Here, too, the sin was caused by an abundance of good.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מָשָׁל לְאָדָם אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ בֵּן. הִרְחִיצוֹ וְסָכוֹ, וְהֶאֱכִילוֹ וְהִשְׁקָהוּ, וְתָלָה לוֹ כִּיס עַל צַוָּארוֹ, וְהוֹשִׁיבוֹ עַל פֶּתַח שֶׁל זוֹנוֹת. מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ הַבֵּן שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא?!
segments.en: The Gemara offers another analogy: «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» This is «comparable to a person who had a son; he bathed him and anointed him» with oil, «fed him and gave him drink, and hung a purse» of money «around his neck.» Then, he «brought» his son «to the entrance of a brothel. What could the son do to avoid sinning?»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי: מְלֵי כְּרֵסֵיהּ זְנֵי בִּישֵׁי. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כְּמַרְעִיתָם וַיִּשְׂבָּעוּ שָׂבְעוּ וַיָּרׇם לִבָּם עַל כֵּן שְׁכֵחוּנִי״. רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: מֵהָכָא: ״וְרָם לְבָבֶךָ וְשָׁכַחְתָּ אֶת ה׳״. וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי, מֵהָכָא: ״וְאָכַל וְשָׂבַע וְדָשֵׁן וּפָנָה״.
segments.en: On a similar note, «Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Huna, said» that «Rav Sheshet said: That is what people say» in a popular maxim: «Filling his stomach is a type of sin, as it is stated: “When they were fed and became full they were sated, and their hearts were lifted and they have forgotten Me”» (Hosea 13:6). «Rav Naḥman said:» This principle is derived not from the verse in Hosea, but «from here: “And your heart is lifted and you forget the Lord”» (Deuteronomy 8:14). «And the Rabbis say» that this principle is derived «from here: “And they will have eaten and been sated and fattened, and they will turn» to other gods” (Deuteronomy 31:20).

segments.he: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא מֵהָכָא: ״וַיִּשְׁמַן יְשׁוּרוּן וַיִּבְעָט״. אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁחָזַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְהוֹדָה לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכֶסֶף הִרְבֵּיתִי לָהֶם וְזָהָב עָשׂוּ לַבָּעַל״.
segments.en: «And if you wish, say» instead that it is derived «from here: “And Jeshurun grew fat and kicked”» (Deuteronomy 32:15). «Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said» that «Rabbi Yonatan said: From where» in the Torah is it derived that «the Holy One, Blessed be He, ultimately conceded to Moses» that the reason for the sin of the Golden Calf was indeed the riches lavished upon Israel? «As it is stated: “And I gave them an abundance of silver and gold, which they used for the Ba’al”» (Hosea 2:10).

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי חמא ברבי חנינא: אלמלא שלש מקראות הללו
moves.summary: R' Chama b. R' Chanina: without three verses the legs of Israel would have collapsed in judgment

moves.cueHe: חד דכתיב
moves.summary: the three verses are listed: 'whom I dealt wickedly', 'clay in the potter's hand', 'I will remove the heart of stone'
moves.about: first of the three verses showing God influences human conduct

moves.cueHe: רב פפא אמר מהכא
moves.summary: Rav Pappa offers a clearer proof from 'I will cause you to walk in My statutes'
moves.about: a clearer proof that God directs human conduct

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי אלעזר: משה הטיח דברים כלפי מעלה
moves.summary: R' Elazar continues his series: Moses too spoke impertinently toward Heaven
moves.about: Moses prayed 'to the Lord' after the murmurers' sin

moves.cueHe: שנאמר: ״ויתפלל משה אל ה׳״
moves.summary: the prooftext 'and Moses prayed to the Lord' is cited
moves.about: read 'al' (onto) for 'el' (to): Moses spoke impertinently toward Heaven

moves.cueHe: אל תקרי ״אל ה׳״ אלא ״על ה׳״
moves.summary: al-tikrei: read 'onto the Lord', the language of impertinence

moves.cueHe: שכן דבי רבי אליעזר בן יעקב קורין
moves.summary: the gemara grounds the alef/ayin interchange in the reading practice of R' Eliezer ben Yaakov's school
moves.about: the school of R' Eliezer ben Yaakov reads alef as ayin and ayin as alef

moves.cueHe: דבי רבי ינאי אמרי, מהכא: ״ודי זהב״
moves.summary: the school of R' Yannai derives Moses' impertinence instead from 'Di Zahav'
moves.about: 'And Di Zahav' as proof that Moses spoke impertinently

moves.cueHe: מאי ״ודי זהב״
moves.summary: the gemara asks what 'Di Zahav' means
moves.about: what 'And Di Zahav' means, there being no place of that name

moves.cueHe: אמרי דבי רבי ינאי: כך אמר משה לפני הקדוש ברוך הוא
moves.summary: Moses pleaded: the silver and gold You lavished until they said 'enough' caused the Calf
moves.about: the meaning of 'Di Zahav': the wealth lavished until they said 'enough' caused the Calf

moves.cueHe: אמרי דבי רבי ינאי: אין ארי נוהם
moves.summary: general principle: a lion roars over a basket of meat, not of straw

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אושעיא: משל לאדם שהיתה לו פרה
moves.summary: parable of the lupine-fed cow that kicks its owner: abundance caused the sin
moves.about: abundance of good is what caused the sin, as the lupine-fed cow kicks its owner

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן: משל
moves.summary: another parable, R' Yochanan's: the pampered son seated at a brothel's door cannot avoid sin
moves.about: the parable of the son bathed, fed, given a purse and seated at a brothel's door

moves.cueHe: אמר רב אחא בריה דרב הונא אמר רב ששת: היינו דאמרי אינשי
moves.summary: Rav Sheshet: the folk maxim that a full belly breeds sin
moves.about: the popular maxim that a full belly is a kind of sin, with its verse

moves.cueHe: שנאמר: ״כמרעיתם וישבעו״
moves.summary: the maxim's prooftext from Hosea
moves.about: the folk maxim 'filling his belly is among the evil kinds' (of sin)

moves.cueHe: רב נחמן אמר: מהכא
moves.summary: Rav Nachman sources the maxim from 'your heart is lifted and you forget the Lord'
moves.about: 'and your heart is lifted and you forget the Lord' as the source of the maxim

moves.cueHe: ורבנן אמרי, מהכא
moves.summary: the Rabbis source it from 'eaten and sated and fattened, and turned'
moves.about: 'and they will have eaten and been sated and fattened, and they will turn' as the source

moves.cueHe: ואי בעית אימא מהכא
moves.summary: or, if you wish, from 'Jeshurun grew fat and kicked'
moves.about: 'Jeshurun grew fat and kicked' as yet another source for the maxim

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי שמואל בר נחמני אמר רבי יונתן: מנין
moves.summary: R' Yonatan asks whence that God conceded Moses' argument
moves.about: whence that God ultimately conceded to Moses that the wealth caused the Calf

moves.cueHe: שנאמר: ״וכסף הרביתי להם וזהב עשו לבעל״
moves.summary: Hosea 2:10 shows God attributing the Baal worship to the silver and gold He gave
moves.about: 'I gave them an abundance of silver and gold, which they used for the Baal' shows God conceded
